newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Chinese boatpeople stranded off Indonesian island.
newsitem.headline: Chinese boatpeople stranded off Indonesian island.

text.p: A boat carrying 70 Chinese men, women and children heading for New Zealand has been stranded by engine trouble off the Indonesian resort island of Lombok, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.
Antara quoted Lieutenant-Colonel Darwinsyah, chief of the Lembar naval base on the east coast of Lombok, as saying the boat arrived on Monday afternoon after trouble with its engine's cooling system.
Darwinsyah said the Indonesian authorities would order the boat to leave as soon as the engine was repaired.
"We will not let people, who have illegally entered our territory stay in our waters for a long period," he said.
Darwinsyah said Indonesian authorities would help fix the boat and provide spare parts but the boatpeople, who are from southern China, would not be allowed to leave the vessel.
Antara quoted a local resident as saying the boatpeople had asked on Friday for food and medicine as several of the party were ill and several children had died during the journey.

In recent years hundreds of boatpeople have travelled through Indonesia's archipelago on their way to Australia or New Zealand. All of those who stated their destination as New Zealand have been detained as illegal immigrants after entering Australian territorial waters.
